papers.title: Molecular engineering stabilizes the commensurate charge density wave state in 1T-TaS2/arginine hybrid superlattices.
papers.abstract: The commensurate charge density wave (CCDW) phase in 1T-TaS2 is a prototypical correlated state tied to diverse emergent quantum phenomena. However, its stability is intrinsically limited to cryogenic temperatures. Tailoring correlated electronic states and stabilizing the CCDW phase at room temperature offer new opportunities to investigate and control emergent phenomena under ambient conditions. Here we report a molecular engineering strategy to modulate the charge density wave (CDW) phases in 1T-TaS2/arginine hybrid superlattices. We show that the intercalated arginine molecules exhibit strong non-covalent interactions with the 1T-TaS2 atomic layers, effectively modulating the correlated electronic phase and increasing the CCDW stabilization temperature to 330 K. In contrast, other weakly interacting amino acids produce a less pronounced modulation of the CDW phase transitions. Computational modelling reveals that arginine molecules reshape the CDW energy landscape, enhancing both the thermodynamic stability and kinetic robustness against thermal fluctuations. These findings establish a versatile molecular engineering strategy for tailoring correlated states and electronic orders in van der Waals materials.

papers.title: Nitrene generation and transfer for unnatural biosynthesis in living cells.
papers.abstract: Synthetic biology has enabled the production of natural and unnatural products from inexpensive sustainable feedstocks. Yet, the scope of available products has been limited largely to compounds accessible from nature's chemical reactions. Evolved enzymes can catalyse reactions of unnatural substrates or reactions not found in nature but often require the addition of synthetic reagents to purified enzymes or to resting cells containing those enzymes. Here we show that chemical reactions of metabolic intermediates produced intracellularly in living cells can include intermolecular nitrene transfers. The biosynthesis of N-acetoxyanilines, in combination with the generation and transfer of N-aryl nitrene intermediates from them catalysed by a cytochrome P450, generates amino alcohols, diamines, diarylamines and aminoalkyl arenes from simple carbon feedstocks. These products-common substructures of pharmaceuticals and agrochemicals-are challenging to synthesize by standard organic chemistry and were produced from inexpensive, renewable feedstocks. Evolution of the enzymes in this pathway showed that titres can be increased by engineering and that the products can be synthesized with high enantioselectivity.

papers.title: Using enantioselective biosensors to evolve asymmetric biocatalysts.
papers.abstract: Biocatalysts are prized for their enantioselectivity, but slow chromatographic separations required to measure enantiomeric excess bottleneck their development. To overcome this limitation, we evolve enantioselective transcription factors (eTFs) that convert enzyme-catalyzed enantiomer concentrations into programmable gene expression outputs, focusing on imine reductases. Here, using a massively parallel reporter assay, we measure dose-response curves for over 300,000 transcription factor variants in response to an imine precursor and chiral amine products. We quantify the sensitivity, selectivity and dynamic range across variants generated by random, site-saturation and shuffling mutagenesis, isolating variants with exceptional specificity. High-resolution structures of evolved eTFs elucidate how steric effects enforce enantioselectivity, while charge interactions distinguish the imine from the amines. Using two eTFs, we create an ultrahigh-throughput chiral screen to evolve an imine reductase with inverted enantioselectivity. To support generalizability and speed, we design a genetic circuit that enables TF generation within weeks. Our methods enable rapid measurement of asymmetric reactions, supporting innovation in chemical manufacturing.

papers.title: Genetic recording and in situ readout of single-cell signaling memory.
papers.abstract: Intensity and duration of biological signals encode a few pathways to direct diverse cellular behaviors, yet quantifying these features in single cells remains difficult. To address this challenge, we developed INSCRIBE, which uses a CRISPR base editor to mutate genomic targets at rates proportional to signaling activity. Edits are recovered at the endpoint through a new ratiometric readout strategy from images of two fluorescence channels. We engineered human cells to record WNT and BMP activity. Following defined exogenous stimulations, INSCRIBE accurately recovered signal intensity in dose-response experiments and exposure duration in time-course experiments. Applying INSCRIBE revealed a persistent memory in the BMP pathway, where progeny of high-responding cells remained more sensitive to subsequent BMP stimulation for up to 3 weeks. Together, our results establish a scalable platform for genetic recording and in situ readout of signaling activity in single cells, advancing quantitative analysis of cell-cell communication during development and disease.

papers.title: Abasic CRISPR RNAs inherently harness fidelity of SpCas9 for genome editing.
papers.abstract: CRISPR-Cas9, an RNA-guided immune system, functions specifically in bacteria while controlling autoimmunity. However, its application to genome editing often causes deleterious off-target cleavages. Here, by sequencing CRISPR RNAs (crRNAs), we discovered abasic modifications that naturally suppress off-target self-cleavages from activated Cas9 in Streptococcus pyogenes (SpCas9). Bacteriophage infection induces oxidative stress, preferentially oxidizing the 5' end of crRNAs into abasic modifications. Mechanistically, abasic substitutions at the 5' end reduce off-target effects by limiting base pairing while preserving SpCas9-interacting backbones to maintain on-target efficiency. Abasic extensions at the 5' end reduce off-target effects by sterically constraining SpCas9 but retain on-target activity by avoiding extra base pairs. Moreover, these approaches can be combined (abasic substitution and extension), enhancing SpCas9 fidelity by increasing mismatch intolerance at the protospacer-adjacent motif-distal region and outperforming SpCas9 variants. Biologically inspired, we developed abasic chemical modifications for guide RNAs that improve CRISPR-Cas9 genome-editing specificity, demonstrating potential for in vivo application.

papers.title: A novel FRET-force biosensor for nucleoporin gp210 reveals that the nuclear pore complex experiences mechanical tension.
papers.abstract: The nuclear pore complex (NPC) is a large multi-protein structure that enables movement of macromolecules, such as mRNA and proteins, between the nucleoplasm and cytoplasm. There has been great interest in how the physical state of the NPC can influence nuclear-cytoplasmic transport. The hypothesis that the NPC may be mechanosensitive is supported by prior reports showing that the diameter of the NPC increases with nuclear envelope stretch as well as increased ECM stiffness. We therefore sought to develop a biosensor-based approach to determine if the NPC experiences mechanical tension. Using a previously developed FRET-force biosensor, known as TSMod, we developed a gp210 tension sensor. gp210 is a transmembrane nucleoporin, which may serve to anchor the NPC into the nuclear envelope. Using a CRISPR knock-in strategy, we developed a HeLa cell line which expresses the gp210 tension sensor at endogenous levels. The FRET-force responsiveness of the gp210 tension sensor was validated using hypo-osmotic and hyper-osmotic nuclear swelling experiments. Additionally, we observed that gp210 forces are sensitive to the ECM, nuclear LINC complex, chromatin condensation, and actomyosin contractility. Our results indicate that both nuclear strain and cytoskeletal forces contribute to mechanical tension across gp210. Our studies provide the first direct measurements of protein-level mechanical forces on the NPC. We anticipate that the gp210 force sensor will be of use for future studies of NPC mechanobiology.

papers.title: Degeneracy in neuronal bifurcation landscapes: Equivalent bifurcation sequences across distinct parameter sets.
papers.abstract: Degeneracy, the capacity of structurally distinct systems to achieve similar functions, is a fundamental property of living organisms, enabling adaptability and resilience. Neurons can maintain stable activity patterns despite substantial variability in ion channel expression, highlighting how different intrinsic configurations can produce equivalent electrophysiological behaviors. Previous studies have shown that neuronal activity emerges from the interaction between intrinsic membrane properties and ionic concentration dynamics. However, how degeneracy is organized within the dynamical landscape of neurons and how different degenerate configurations respond to external perturbations remain poorly understood. Here, we investigate how distinct biophysical parameter sets generate equivalent bifurcation sequences and how their resilience changes under ionic modulation. Using a minimal neuron model with three variable conductances, we systematically explore how variations in extracellular potassium concentration, representing physiological and pathological conditions, reshape neuronal dynamics. We show that distinct conductance configurations occupy structured regions of parameter space that support the same bifurcation pathways, leading to equivalent activity regimes such as bursting, seizure-like activity, and depolarization block. However, these degenerate configurations exhibit different sensitivities to extracellular perturbations, revealing that functional equivalence under fixed conditions does not imply equivalent robustness. To quantify this effect, we introduce resilience as a measure of the threshold at which a given conductance configuration transitions into a specific activity regime under external ionic changes. Our results demonstrate that degeneracy extends beyond the coexistence of multiple solutions: degenerate configurations form structured landscapes with distinct trajectories under environmental modulation. This framework provides a quantitative approach to investigate how intrinsic variability influences neuronal vulnerability and resilience across different dynamical states.

papers.title: ATP-independent entropy-driven dsRNA unwinding by DDX3X revealed by coarse-grained simulations and deep learning.
papers.abstract: DEAD-box RNA helicases (DDXs) are traditionally known as ATP-dependent motors that unwind double-stranded RNA (dsRNA). Recent experiments, however, show that some DDXs promote dsRNA unwinding even in the absence of ATP, raising a fundamental question about the physical mechanism underlying ATP-independent strand separation. Here, we develop a minimal, physics-based coarse-grained RNA model and incorporate weak, specific interactions between DDX3X and dsRNA, revealing the inherently stochastic nature of unwinding events. The unwinding process must overcome an energy barrier, but thermal fluctuations and entropy gain provide a driving force for RNA remodeling. We identify that dsRNA separation proceeds through rare yet obligatory strand-displacing intermediates facilitated by DDX3X. By combining deep learning-assisted analysis, we further rank the contributions of different entropic components, revealing hydrogen bonding as the dominant factor, followed by base stacking and then the backbone conformation. These findings reveal a previously unrecognized physical mechanism for RNA duplex unwinding and offer an effective framework for studying RNA remodeling kinetics.

papers.title: Coupled beta and high-frequency oscillations emerge from synchronized bursting in a minimal model of the parkinsonian subthalamic nucleus.
papers.abstract: Local field potentials (LFPs) recorded from the subthalamic nucleus (STN) in Parkinson's disease (PD) exhibit a distinctive multiscale spectral signature: exaggerated beta-band oscillations (13-30 Hz) coupled to high-frequency oscillations (HFOs, 200-400 Hz), with HFO amplitude being phase-locked to the beta cycle. This phase-amplitude coupling (PAC) has been identified as a promising biomarker of the parkinsonian state, yet no biophysical model has explained how it emerges, what determines the HFO frequency, or how HFOs can exist without beta modulation in the medicated STN. Here we show that a heterogeneous population of excitatory Izhikevich neurons with recurrent coupling produces three dynamical regimes: (i) asynchronous tonic firing, (ii) asynchronous bursting, in which neurons burst individually producing broadband HFO power but without coherent population-level PAC, and (iii) synchronous bursting, which gives rise to beta-HFO PAC. The regimes are governed by two biophysically interpretable parameters that capture complementary effects of dopamine depletion: one reflecting changes in intrinsic neuronal excitability, the other reflecting changes in synaptic coupling strength. The transition from asynchronous to synchronous bursting in this model emulates the emergence of pathological STN neuronal activity in the parkinsonian state. HFO peak frequency varies continuously across the two-parameter landscape, suggesting a possible mechanism of the clinically observed shift from slow (200-300 Hz) to fast (300-400 Hz) HFOs between medication states. The character of the synchronization transition depends on baseline excitability, ranging from a sharp co-emergence of bursting and synchrony at low excitability to a decoupled transition at intermediate excitability, where the bursting fraction saturates while the population synchronization continues to increase with coupling. The asynchronous-to-synchronous bursting transition and the beta-HFO PAC in the STN population also arise in an extended version of the model with reciprocal coupling to an inhibitory population of globus pallidus externa (GPe)-like neurons, with the beta frequency varying with the delay in the synaptic coupling between the two populations. The model generates testable predictions for future clinical and experimental studies, provides a numerical dissection of how mesoscopic LFP features could map onto microscopic neuronal dynamics, and serves as a computational building block for future circuit-level models that may inform brain stimulation strategies tailored to the patient-specific dynamical state of the STN.

papers.title: A dual-targeting lipid nanoparticle delivery system for precision phage therapy against multidrug-resistant Gram-negative bacteria.
papers.abstract: The escalating crisis of antimicrobial resistance, particularly among Gram-negative bacteria, demands innovative therapeutic strategies. Here, we present a dual-targeting lipid nanoparticle-chimeric phage (AbLCP) system engineered to combat multidrug-resistant (MDR) Gram-negative bacteria. Our design integrates a genetically modified M13 phage displaying anti-lipopolysaccharide (LPS) antibodies with polymyxin B conjugation, which is further encapsulated within anti-LPS antibody-functionalized lipid nanoparticles. This system overcomes the fundamental limitations of conventional phage therapy, enabling efficient cellular internalization, endosomal escape, and potent intracellular bactericidal activity. In murine models of Pseudomonas aeruginosa infection, AbLCP achieved superior bacterial clearance and up to 103-fold reduction in bacterial burden at a 103-fold lower effective dose than free polymyxin B, with 67-fold selective accumulation at infection sites, and attenuated systemic inflammation and preservation of gut microbiota. Mechanistically, AbLCP neutralized LPS to suppress inflammation and induced a lethal bacterial stress response. This work establishes a transformative nanophage platform that merges synthetic biology with nanomedicine, offering a promising strategy against MDR bacterial infections.

papers.title: FOSL1-associated condensates modulate superenhancer-mediated selected IL-1 family gene activation in psoriasis.
papers.abstract: Psoriasis is a chronic inflammatory skin disease involving abnormal keratinocyte gene expression, yet the upstream epigenetic mechanisms driving these alterations remain unclear. papers.title: Intrinsic stochasticity in cell polarity and contact inhibition of locomotion.
papers.abstract: When cells collide, they often exhibit "contact inhibition of locomotion" (CIL), a behavior in which cells repolarize and migrate away from the site of contact. Experimental CIL outcomes are highly variable-why? Here, we develop a minimal stochastic model to quantify how intrinsic noise in cell polarity, arising from the finite number of signaling molecules, influences CIL decision-making. We simulate polarization dynamics by tracking individual Rho GTPase proteins that diffuse and switch stochastically between the cell membrane and cytosol. In the absence of cell-cell contact, the polarity axis diffuses rotationally-the cell's orientation wanders-with a diffusion coefficient that decreases as Rho GTPase copy number increases. Assuming that cell-cell contact inhibits Rho GTPase activation, we investigate how contact geometry, duration, and strength affect CIL sensitivity. At low protein copy number, weak, brief, or spatially narrow contacts are masked by molecular noise. In contrast, at high protein copy number, intrinsic polarity noise is negligible, and randomness in CIL response is more likely to reflect the variability from collision to collision in the cell-cell contact properties.

papers.title: Enhanced Quantitative Accuracy in Single Molecule Imaging: A Fidelity-Guided Denoising Approach.
papers.abstract: Single-molecule total internal reflection fluorescence (TIRF) microscopy provides unparalleled insight into biological processes, but reaches fundamental limits due to the challenges of imaging individual fluorophores, where limited photon counts mean signals often border background noise. Practically, trade-offs exist between emission rate, time resolution, and observation lifetime. Experimentalists increasingly seek higher time resolution and longer observational times, demanding accurate quantification of fluorescence intensity and super-resolved positional information. Consequently, single-molecule detection must operate at low signal-to-noise ratios, often requiring significant human oversight to optimize. Applying machine learning to improve signal-to-noise would reduce these analytical bottlenecks, allowing researchers to work at lower photon counts to further push observational limits. However, while existing computational methods enhance traditional fluorescent microscopy, single-molecule analysis presents a unique challenge: the benefits of denoising often come at the unacceptable cost of distorting the vital positional and brightness measurements. We address this critical trade-off with an intelligent deep learning-based denoising framework guided by a fidelity constraint, preventing the algorithm from creating artifacts or distorting molecular features. Our training objective is informed by the calibrated Poisson-Gaussian noise model of the detector. This cleans images, easing spot detection while preserving absolute intensity and positional data. Additionally, we present a version in which a reinforcement learning agent sets the strength of this constraint automatically during training, removing the need for manual parameter exploration. On simulated data, our approach raises the single-molecule detection F1-Score from 0.10 to 0.63 under the most challenging noise conditions tested, while preserving molecular features. Finally, on experimental data of fluorescently-labelled, membrane-interacting peptides, our method reduces errors in measuring molecular position by a factor of two to five and a half, and changes the measured brightness four to thirteen times less, compared to leading denoising methods.

papers.title: A Biophysical Framework for Force-Induced Mitochondrial Branches.
papers.abstract: Mitochondrial networks are shaped not only by fission and fusion but also by mechanical forces. Here, we examine pulling-induced branch formation and contrast it with fusion-based branch formation. Live imaging reveals that branches formed by pulling are shorter-lived but initiate more frequently and with a narrower range of angles, concomitantly inducing deformation in parent mitochondria - in contrast with those formed by fusion. In addition, perturbations to microtubule stability and motor protein association with mitochondria alter pulled branch lifetimes, emphasizing the role of cytoskeletal dynamics in branch stability. We developed a mechanical model based on free energy minimization that predicts branch thickness as a function of pulling force, membrane tension, and mitochondrial geometry. Our model suggests that forces in the range of single motor proteins (0-4 pN) can account for the experimentally observed branch formation. Finally, STED microscopy reveals that pulling-induced branches preferentially initiate in regions of low cristae density, potentially due to their reduced mechanical resistance. These regions often contain mitochondrial nucleoids, which are rearranged during branch formation. Together, our findings highlight an underappreciated role for force-induced membrane deformation in shaping mitochondrial architecture and provide a framework for understanding similar remodeling processes in other tubular organelles.

papers.title: Enhanced cfDNA methylation profiling by detection and correction of jagged ends.
papers.abstract: Analysis of cell-free DNA (cfDNA) methylation can enable noninvasive disease detection by leveraging tissue-specific epigenetic differences between malignant and nonmalignant cells. However, such analyses can be confounded by the repair of jagged DNA fragment ends during double-stranded sequencing library preparation, which introduces spurious methylation signals into cfDNA molecules. Here we present JEEPERS, a framework to detect and correct jagged-end-induced methylation errors while preserving duplex integrity and native methylation patterns. We showed high fidelity for measuring tumor burden and demonstrated allele-specific methylation differences at recurrent somatic mutations, revealing a link between adjacent CpG methylation and EGFR/TP53 driver and resistance mutations. We further demonstrated enhanced diagnostic performance across liquid biopsy applications, including tumor-type-specific methylation profiles, hemimethylation profiling, epigenetic-clock-based age estimation and cell type deconvolution. By faithfully correcting end-repair errors, JEEPERS provides a versatile framework for integrating mutations and methylation features in cfDNA at high resolution, enabling more precise molecular profiling and disease monitoring.

papers.title: Metax enables accurate cross-domain taxonomic profiling of metagenomes.
papers.abstract: Taxonomic profiling is fundamental to microbiome research, yet achieving high species-level accuracy remains challenging for complex communities that span bacteria, viruses, eukaryotes, and archaea, and these limitations are exacerbated in low-biomass, host-dominated samples. Across >600 samples from host-associated, environmental, wastewater, and low-biomass clinical settings, including benchmarks with limited reference representation, Metax improved profiling accuracy, achieving on average 55% higher F1 scores and 45% lower Bray-Curtis dissimilarity than other methods. Moreover, this broad evaluation demonstrated that Metax resolved bacterial and viral signatures of peri-implantitis in oral microbiomes and revealed signals suggestive of reagent-borne contaminants and reference misassemblies in plasma-cell-free DNA. By leveraging genome-wide coverage evidence, Metax enables robust cross-domain profiling across diverse sample types and sequencing depths, including settings where reference databases are highly incomplete.

papers.title: Connectome simulations identify a central pattern generator for fly walking.
papers.abstract: Animal locomotion relies on rhythmic body movements driven by central pattern generators (CPGs): neural circuits that produce oscillating output without oscillating input. Simulations also predicted that a separate descending pathway (DNb08) drives rhythmic leg movements, which we confirmed experimentally using optogenetics in behaving flies. Our results reveal the cellular identity and synaptic structure of a putative CPG circuit for walking and other rhythmic leg movements in flies.

papers.title: Clostridium perfringens Delta toxin targets CD9 to drive NEC and brain injury.
papers.abstract: Necrotizing enterocolitis (NEC) is the most devastating gastrointestinal emergency in preterm infants, frequently causing mortality and long-term neurodevelopmental impairment1,2. Clinically, infected infants show worse outcomes, including aberrant systemic inflammation, severe neurological damage and coagulopathy. We establish a mouse model in which Delta-toxin-positive C. perfringens infection, or Delta toxin exposure alone, recapitulates clinical features of NEC, including intestinal necrosis and acute cerebral injury. Mechanistically, Delta toxin preferentially targets macrophages, potently activating inflammasome signalling and pyroptosis, triggering a rapid inflammatory cascade that compromises blood-brain barrier integrity and drives neuroinflammation. Furthermore, a neutralizing anti-Delta toxin monoclonal antibody confers protection against disease progression. papers.title: An engineered, compact Cas12m variant for multiplexed gene activation in vivo.
papers.abstract: Achieving coordinated CRISPR-based transactivation (CRISPRa) regulation in vivo remains challenging, as the requisite genetic elements frequently exceed the packaging capacity of AAV vectors. Here we report the identification and engineering of the Cas12m protein family, a naturally nuclease-dead CRISPR system that possesses intrinsic self-processing activity for its precursor crRNA. We develop an optimized variant, denCas12m, and leverage it in the smCRISPRa platform. We show that a single transcriptional unit encoding a multi-gRNA array can be processed into individual functional guides within a target cell, enabling efficient synergistic activation of a single gene through multiple sites or simultaneous activation of distinct endogenous genes from a single all-in-one AAV vector. We demonstrate phenotypic rescue in mouse models of Duchenne muscular dystrophy and Scn1a haploinsufficiency. Furthermore, a single all-in-one AAV vector supports the simultaneous activation of multiple distinct endogenous genes in mice, with a single vector delivering up to eight crRNAs for activation of six different genes, demonstrating the platform's high-order multiplexing.

papers.title: Strand- and replication timing-dependent functions of DNA polymerase η in human DNA replication.
papers.abstract: Efficient DNA replication requires coordinated use of replicative and error-prone polymerases, which provide flexibility at the cost of mutagenesis. DNA polymerase η (Pol η) tolerates UV-induced lesions via translesion synthesis (TLS), but may contribute more broadly to DNA synthesis. Using polymerase usage sequencing (Pu-seq), we map Pol η activity genome-wide during unperturbed replication in human cells. Pol η preferentially participates in lagging strand replication, as in budding yeast. This bias requires direct PCNA interaction, suggesting stochastic engagement of PCNA-bound intermediates at replication forks. Pol η usage also varies across S phase, with PCNA ubiquitylation-dependent enrichment in late-replicating domains. In cancer genomes, characteristic Pol η mutations are enriched in late-replicating regions and correlate with RAD18 expression, linking PCNA ubiquitylation to Pol η-mediated mutagenesis. Thus, Pol η usage is biased by strand and replication timing during unperturbed replication and may contribute to mutational burden in human genomes.

papers.title: Modeling reaction-diffusion processes in simplified to complex astroglial branchlet geometries using different simulation tools.
papers.abstract: Computational modeling of spatial biochemical processes in neuroscience is increasingly important as advances in experimental and imaging techniques provide detailed insights into cellular organization. Reaction-diffusion models are commonly used to study the diffusion and interactions of ions and molecules within neuronal cells, and multiple open-access simulation platforms have been developed to support such analysis. However, a comprehensive analysis of commonly used simulation tools, including MCell, STEPS, NeuroRD, and NEURON, remains lacking, particularly for realistic glial cell geometries, as these tools were originally developed for neurons. Here, we present a systematic analysis of these four simulation environments by implementing equivalent calcium diffusion and calcium-calmodulin reaction-diffusion models across a range of spatial domains. These include simplified geometries (cylinders and rectangular cuboids) as well as biologically realistic astroglial morphologies derived from electron microscopy data, including mouse Bergmann glia and mouse and human cortical astrocytes. Using matched kinetic parameters and diffusion constants, we examine simulation outputs and morphological variations across platforms under comparable conditions. We find that all tools produce overall consistent results for the systems considered, indicating that each can reliably capture diffusion and reaction-diffusion dynamics in simplified and complex geometries. At the same time, we show that the structural heterogeneity of branchlets from human astrocytes and mouse Bergmann glia gives rise to distinct calcium signaling, demonstrating that fine-scale morphology critically shapes astroglial dynamics and must be accurately captured by simulation frameworks. In addition, notable differences emerge in geometry representation, implementation strategies, computational aspects, and usability of the tools. By highlighting key trade-offs between geometric fidelity, flexibility, and computational cost in modeling intracellular biochemical processes, these findings provide practical guidance for selecting appropriate simulation tools. More broadly, our results support the use of reaction-diffusion modeling in morphologically realistic astrocytic environments and contribute to enabling mechanistic studies of localized signaling events at synaptic and perisynaptic sites.

papers.title: The evolutionary advantage of replacers in the Moran process.
papers.abstract: Evolution occurs in populations of reproducing individuals. In stochastic descriptions of evolutionary dynamics, such as the Moran process, individuals are chosen randomly for birth and for death. If the same type is chosen for both steps, then the reproductive event is wasted, because the composition of the population remains unchanged. Here we introduce a new phenotype, which we call a replacer. Replacers are efficient competitors. When a replacer is chosen for reproduction, the offspring will always replace an individual of another type (if available). We determine the selective advantage of replacers in well-mixed populations and on one-dimensional lattices. We find that being a replacer substantially boosts the fixation probability of neutral and deleterious mutants. In particular, fixation probability of a single neutral replacer who invades a well-mixed population of size N is of the order of 1/N rather than the standard 1/N. Even more importantly, replacers are much better protected against invasions once they have reached fixation. Therefore, replacers dominate the mutation selection equilibrium even if the phenotype of being a replacer comes at a substantial cost: curiously, for large population sizes and small mutation rates, the relative reproductive rate of a successful replacer can be as low as 1/e.

papers.title: Out-of-balance growth enables cost-free synthesis of the flagellum and other proteins in a single bacterium.
papers.abstract: The cost of expressing unnecessary genes on growth has been explained at the population level through balanced growth assumptions. However, due to the high degree of stochasticity in growth and gene regulation, it remains unclear how classical growth laws derived from bulk measurements manifest at the level of individual cells. For example, flagellar gene expression, one of the most energy-intensive processes in Escherichia coli, is typically associated with reduced growth rates in bulk measurements. By contrast, we find at the single-cell level that a strikingly opposite behavior coexists: flagellar gene activity is associated with an increase in growth rate. We show that this apparent contradiction, reminiscent of Simpson's paradox, results from examining in each cell instantaneous growth and gene expression without indiscriminately aggregating the single-cell data like in bulk measurements. We attribute this unrecognized behavior to out-of-balance growth boosts that temporarily offset the burden of flagellum production, likely driven by a surplus of growth factors inherited across cell division. Furthermore, we show that this non-intuitive relationship between growth and gene expression at the single-cell level is general, as we observe similar effects with synthetic systems driving the expression of fluorescent proteins downstream of constitutive promoters. Finally, we use a computational model to show that the inheritance of parental growth factors can explain the apparent contradiction and constitutes a general mechanism for mitigating the short-term cost of nonessential and biosynthetically demanding genes in the single cell.

papers.title: OSCAR: an omics atlas of paired single-cell ATAC-seq and RNA-seq for decoding cell-specific gene regulation.
papers.abstract: Paired single-cell chromatin accessibility and transcriptome profiles provide a powerful framework for dissecting cell-specific regulatory programs underlying diverse biological processes and human diseases. The rapid accumulation of paired single-cell assay for transposase-accessible chromatin sequencing (scATAC-seq) and single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) data has led to an urgent need to comprehensively integrate these data to illustrate the regulatory landscape at single-cell resolution. To address this need, we developed OSCAR (an Omics atlas of paired Single-Cell ATAC and RNA-seq, https://bio.liclab.net/OSCAR/) to curate large-scale paired scATAC-seq and scRNA-seq data and to provide comprehensive regulatory annotations and analyses. The current version of OSCAR catalogs 7749 898 human cells from 1136 samples across 30 tissue types. Importantly, OSCAR integrates paired scATAC-seq and scRNA-seq profiles for joint cell clustering and peak-to-gene linkage identification, and provides detailed (epi)genetic annotations for marker peaks and regulatory elements of marker genes, including super-enhancers, enhancers, enhancer RNAs (eRNAs), common and risk single nucleotide polymorphisms, expression quantitative trait loci, transcription factor binding sites, transcription factor/transcription co-factor binding peaks, Clustered Regularly Interspaced Short Palindromic Repeats (CRISPR)/Cas9 target sites, DNase I hypersensitivity sites, chromatin accessibility regions, DNA methylation sites, chromatin interaction regions, and topologically associating domains. Furthermore, OSCAR provides three online analysis tools, including cell type enrichment analysis, sequence-based peak regulatory analysis, and peak-to-gene linkage analysis. Hence, OSCAR is a useful platform to query, browse, analyze, and visualize cell-specific regulatory programs across diverse human tissues and diseases.

papers.title: SynBioFooDB: a comprehensive resource for synthetic biology-driven food biomanufacturing.
papers.abstract: Enabled by synthetic biology and metabolic engineering, microbial biomanufacturing is reshaping the production of food-related compounds by offering sustainable alternatives to resource-intensive extraction and conventional chemical synthesis. However, information linking food-related compounds to biosynthetic pathways and microbial biomanufacturing evidence remains fragmented across the literature and poorly represented in existing food-oriented resources, hindering cross-study comparison, evidence synthesis, and rational design of microbial production systems. Here, we present SynBioFooDB (https://synbiofoodb.biodesign.ac.cn/), a knowledgebase dedicated to synthetic biology-driven food biomanufacturing. SynBioFooDB integrates 74 237 food-related compounds with standardized chemical identities and annotations covering food occurrence, bioactivity, toxicity, and regulatory information. It further provides expert-curated biomanufacturing evidence for 1054 compounds from 5592 publications, linking microbial hosts, substrates, genetic modifications, and quantitative production metrics through structured and traceable records. The database also contains 2002 literature-reported biosynthetic pathways for 971 compounds, enabling comparison of alternative precursors, enzyme combinations, and pathway architectures. For compounds without literature-reported pathways, SynBioFooDB provides computationally predicted candidate pathways to facilitate pathway prioritization and experimental evaluation. By integrating compound-level context, biomanufacturing evidence, and biosynthetic pathway information, SynBioFooDB supports systematic exploration, comparison, and rational design of microbial production strategies for food-related compounds.

papers.title: Emergence of chiral multi-armed spirals in an open system of migrating cells under continuous cell supply.
papers.abstract: From molecular assemblies to multicellular tissues, chirality organizes living and active-matter systems into striking collective states. Across cellular collectives and active materials, weak microscopic chiral cues in motion and interaction can systematically skew how constituents coordinate, flow, and break spatial symmetries. Yet the principles that govern chiral ordering in open systems, where elements are continuously supplied and removed, remain poorly understood. Here, we show that chemotaxis-deficient Dictyostelium discoideum mutants (KI cells) form centimeter-scale, clockwise, multi-armed spirals. Each arm is a traveling band produced by short-range alignment interactions and guided by a polar-ordered rotating core that encircles the cell source. A subtle clockwise bias in single-cell migration is amplified by collective ordering into tissue-scale chirality. To uncover the minimal ingredients, we developed an open chiral Vicsek model and found that intrinsic chirality, polar alignment, and continuous cell supply are the key factors. Our study establishes a general route by which weak microscopic chirality and sustained material flux generate macroscopic chiral order, offering new insight into chiral patterning in multicellular systems.
papers.abstract_zh: 从分子组装到多细胞组织，手性将生命与活性物质系统组织成引人注目的集体状态。在细胞集体和活性材料中，运动与相互作用中微弱的微观手性线索能够系统性地影响组分的协调、流动和空间对称性破缺。然而，在组分被持续供给和移除的开放系统中，支配手性有序化的原理仍知之甚少。本研究表明，趋化缺陷型盘基网柄菌突变体（KI细胞）可形成厘米级、顺时针的多臂螺旋。每条臂是由短程对齐相互作用产生的行进带，并受围绕细胞源、具有极性有序的旋转核心引导。单细胞迁移中微弱的顺时针偏好在集体有序化作用下被放大为组织尺度的手性。为揭示最小要素，我们建立了开放手性Vicsek模型，发现内在手性、极性对齐和持续细胞供给是关键因素。本研究确立了一条由微弱微观手性与持续物质流生成宏观手性序的通用路径，为多细胞系统中的手性图案形成提供了新见解。
key_findings: 趋化缺陷型KI细胞形成厘米级顺时针多臂螺旋，臂由短程对齐和极性旋转核心引导。
单细胞微弱顺时针偏好经集体有序化放大为组织尺度手性。
开放手性Vicsek模型揭示内在手性、极性对齐和持续细胞供给是关键因素。

llm_filter.reason: 开发开放手性Vicsek模型，揭示弱微观手性经集体有序放大为宏观手性的普适机制，具备方法学迁移价值。

papers.title: Shared α-helix chimeraffibodies enable linker-free bispecific protein design.
papers.abstract: Small protein scaffolds enable precise targeting but often rely on flexible linkers that increase conformational heterogeneity and immunogenic liabilities. Here we develop Chimeraffibodies (CABs), a linker-free bispecific scaffold class that encodes interdomain geometry through seamless α-helix sharing. CABs are designed by AlphaSync, a structure-design framework that defines domain orientation through closed-form exhaustive local rigid-body superposition and ProteinMPNN-based sequence refinement. Using HER2-binding affibody and an albumin-binding domain, we generated 861CM, which preserved parental paratopes while enforcing a defined shared-helix architecture. Structural, biophysical and cellular analyses demonstrated stable assembly, cooperative target recruitment and retained affinity, with HSA binding of ∼14.3 pM and HER2 binding of 610 pM in the albumin-bound state. In vivo imaging revealed sustained tumor localization, reduced hepatic and renal background and improved organ-to-tumor contrast. CABs establish helix sharing as a geometry-encoded strategy for generating compact, homogeneous, and pharmacokinetically optimized bispecific proteins.
papers.abstract_zh: 小蛋白支架可实现精准靶向，但通常依赖柔性连接子，这会增加构象异质性和免疫原性风险。我们开发了嵌合亲和体（Chimeraffibody，CAB），一种无连接子的双特异性支架类型，通过无缝α螺旋共享编码结构域间几何构型。CAB由AlphaSync设计，该结构设计框架通过闭式穷举局部刚体叠加和基于ProteinMPNN的序列优化来确定结构域取向。利用HER2结合亲和体（affibody）和白蛋白结合结构域，我们生成了861CM，它在保持亲本互补位的同时，强制形成确定的共享螺旋结构。结构、生物物理和细胞分析表明其组装稳定、可协同招募靶标并保留亲和力，白蛋白结合状态下HSA结合约14.3 pM，HER2结合610 pM。体内成像显示其肿瘤定位持久，肝脏和肾脏背景降低，器官-肿瘤对比度改善。CAB确立了螺旋共享作为一种几何编码策略，用于生成紧凑、均一且药代动力学优化的双特异性蛋白。

AlphaSync设计的861CM保持亲本结合位点，可稳定组装并协同招募靶标
861CM HSA结合约14.3 pM、HER2结合610 pM，体内肿瘤定位持久、肝肾背景低

papers.title: Open source laser-scanning photostimulation for neuroscience with Zapit.
papers.abstract: Optogenetic tools are indispensable for understanding the causal neural mechanisms underlying animal behavior, providing millisecond-precision control over genetically defined neural populations. Random-access laser-scanning optogenetics is a powerful and underutilized method for transiently manipulating cortical activity in mice. Despite the utility of this technique, no general-purpose open-source implementation currently exists, and potential users need expertise across optics, real-time hardware control, and programming. This represents a major barrier to adoption, particularly for newly established research groups. Here we present 'Zapit', the first open-source general-purpose platform for random-access laser-scanning optogenetic experiments in head-fixed mice. Zapit is fully documented, has a user-friendly GUI, works in stereotaxic coordinates, and comes with easy-to-build hardware options that extend functionality beyond any published system. We validate Zapit's performance through electrophysiological recordings and cortical photoinhibition in behaving mice. Zapit is a novel and innovative tool with the potential to democratize laser-scanning optogenetics and significantly increase uptake throughout the scientific community.
papers.abstract_zh: 光遗传学工具对于理解动物行为背后的因果神经机制不可或缺，可对遗传限定的神经群体实现毫秒级精确控制。随机访问激光扫描光遗传学是一种强大但未充分利用的方法，用于瞬时操控小鼠皮层活动。尽管该技术实用，目前尚无通用的开源实现，潜在用户需要具备光学、实时硬件控制和编程方面的专业知识。这构成了采用该技术的主要障碍，尤其是对新成立的研究组而言。在此我们介绍“Zapit”，这是首个用于头部固定小鼠随机访问激光扫描光遗传学实验的开源通用平台。Zapit 文档齐全，具有用户友好的图形界面，可在立体定位坐标下工作，并提供易于构建的硬件选项，其功能超越了任何已发表系统。我们通过电生理记录和行为中小鼠的皮层光抑制验证了 Zapit 的性能。Zapit 是一个新颖且创新的工具，有望使激光扫描光遗传学大众化，并显著提高整个科学界的应用。
key_findings: 开发了首个开源通用平台Zapit，用于头部固定小鼠的随机访问激光扫描光遗传实验。
Zapit具备完整文档、友好图形界面和立体定位坐标，硬件易构建且功能超越现有系统。
通过电生理记录和行为小鼠皮层光抑制验证性能，有望推动激光扫描光遗传学普及。

papers.title: Calsequestrin localization at RyR2 clusters enables calcium wave propagation in ventricular myocytes.
papers.abstract: Intracellular calcium waves in cardiac myocytes propagate through a fire-diffuse-fire mechanism in which calcium released from one RyR2 cluster diffuses to neighboring clusters and triggers their activation. Yet propagation faces a fundamental physical difficulty: the calcium signal must cross distances of 1-2 μm between Z-planes while being attenuated by cytosolic buffering and diffusion, and at the same time the release site depletes its local sarcoplasmic reticulum calcium store. How waves propagate efficiently despite these constraints has remained unclear. We developed a three-dimensional computational model of mouse ventricular myocytes at submicrometer resolution to address this question. Our central finding is that co-localization of calsequestrin2 (CASQ2) with RyR2 clusters is required for robust wave propagation. In a physiological model, where CASQ2 is concentrated at release sites as observed experimentally, calcium waves propagate reliably across the cell with velocities that match the experimental range. In contrast, when CASQ2 is distributed uniformly throughout the sarcoplasmic reticulum, keeping total CASQ2 unchanged, the wavefront stalls. These results identify CASQ2-RyR2 co-localization as a key structural requirement for effective calcium wave propagation in ventricular myocytes.
key_findings: 开发了亚微米分辨率的小鼠心室肌细胞三维计算模型，用于研究钙波传播机制。
发现CASQ2与RyR2簇共定位是稳健钙波传播所必需的结构条件。
CASQ2集中于释放位点使波速与实验相符，而均匀分布则导致波前停滞。

llm_filter.reason: 开发3D亚微米计算模型揭示CASQ2-RyR2共定位是钙波传播的关键结构要求，具有可迁移的钙信号机制洞察。

papers.title: An integrative computational approach for obstacle avoidance during action selection.
papers.abstract: Action selection in cluttered environments, where individuals must simultaneously pursue goals and avoid obstacles, presents a significant challenge for the brain. To understand the underlying mechanisms of action selection in such contexts, we propose a computational model that extends stochastic optimal control theory through a novel framework for obstacle avoidance. The model decomposes action selection into a weighted combination of individual control policies, each generated for either target approach or obstacle avoidance. By integrating value information from goals, obstacles, and actions into a unified measure of "relative desirability", the model dynamically determines the contribution of each policy to the overall action selection process. We evaluated the framework using simulated target-reaching tasks in cluttered environments based on previous human studies. The results showed that the model qualitatively captures key features of human motor behavior, including the influence of obstacle properties on movement trajectories and the transient tendency to initiate movements toward obstacles before avoidance. This work offers new insights into the dynamic interaction between approach and avoidance behaviors, providing a basis for future studies of action selection in more complex and naturalistic settings.
papers.abstract_zh: 在杂乱环境中，个体必须同时追求目标并避开障碍物，这种动作选择对大脑而言是一项重大挑战。为理解此类情境下动作选择的潜在机制，我们提出了一个计算模型，通过一种新颖的避障框架扩展了随机最优控制理论。该模型将动作选择分解为多个单独控制策略的加权组合，每个策略分别针对目标接近或障碍规避生成。通过将来自目标、障碍物和动作的价值信息整合到一个统一的“相对合意度”度量中，模型动态确定每个策略对整体动作选择过程的贡献。我们基于先前的人类研究，在杂乱环境中的模拟目标到达任务上评估了该框架。结果表明，该模型能够定性捕捉人类运动行为的关键特征，包括障碍物属性对运动轨迹的影响，以及在规避之前朝向障碍物发起运动的瞬时倾向。这项工作为趋近与回避行为之间的动态交互提供了新见解，并为未来在更复杂和自然场景中研究动作选择奠定了基础。
key_findings: 提出基于随机最优控制的避障计算模型，将动作选择分解为目标接近与避障策略的加权组合。
引入“相对合意度”统一度量，整合目标、障碍物与动作价值信息，动态决定各策略贡献。
模型模拟复现人类运动关键特征：障碍物属性影响轨迹，以及初始朝向障碍物再回避的瞬时倾向。

llm_filter.reason: 提出扩展随机最优控制的新计算框架，将目标趋近与障碍回避策略动态加权，具有可迁移的方法学价值
